facts.statement: Yunguisaurus is an extinct genus of pistosaur found in Guizhou Province, China.
facts.quote: Yunguisaurus is an extinct genus of pistosaur known from the Guizhou Province of China.

facts.statement: The holotype of Yunguisaurus is an articulated, almost complete skeleton that lacks only the distal tail.
facts.quote: Yunguisaurus is known from the holotype NMNS 004529/F003862, an articulated and almost complete skeleton missing only the distal tail.

facts.statement: The preserved holotype skeleton measures about 1.7 meters, with an estimated total length of 2.3 meters, while a larger paratype specimen reaches around 4.2 meters.
facts.quote: The preserved skeleton has a length of about 1.7 m with estimated total length about 2.3 m, while paratype specimen became much larger with length around 4.2 m.

facts.statement: Fossils were collected near the Huangnihe River in Chajiang, Guizhou, from the Falang Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected near Huangnihe River, Chajiang of Guizhou, from the Falang Formation.

facts.statement: Yunguisaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the early Late Triassic.
facts.quote: It is thought to belong to the Paragondolella naantangensis-P. polygnathiformis Assemblage Zone, dating to the Carnian stage of the early Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Yunguisaurus was first named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Tamaki Sato, Xiao-Chun Wu, and Chun Li in 2006, with Yunguisaurus liae as the type species.
facts.quote: Yunguisaurus was first named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Tamaki Sato, Xiao-Chun Wu and Chun Li in 2006 and the type species is Yunguisaurus liae.

facts.statement: The generic name Yunguisaurus is derived from the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau, abbreviated as the Yungi Plateau.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Yunnan–Guizhou Plateau (), a landform named after the Yunnan and Guizhou provinces that is also abbreviated as the Yungi Plateau.

facts.statement: The suffix 'saurus' in the name means 'lizard' in Greek.
The specific name liae honors Professor Jinling Li for his contributions to the study of Chinese Triassic marine vertebrate fauna.
facts.quote: The specific name honors IVPP Professor Jinling Li for contributing to the recent study of the Chinese Triassic marine vertebrate fauna.

facts.statement: Yunguisaurus is distinguished from other pistosauroids by a unique combination of anatomical characters.
facts.quote: It differs from other pistosauroids by a combination of characters.

facts.statement: The original description of Yunguisaurus remains a preliminary report because the postcranial skeleton has not yet been fully prepared or described.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, its original description is a preliminary report while the postcranial skeleton still waits for further preparation and full description.

facts.statement: Yunguisaurus belongs to the parent group Pistosauroidea.
Yunguisaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Yunguisaurus lived between 241.464 and 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)
